Well I kinda liked this album. I haven't listened to anything from The New Reign except for Now Arise, but if the rest of that album sounds like that song, then this new album seems to have taken a similar path. Something that I noticed about halfway through was the lack of sweeping and djenting, and the increase of riffing. This was interesting, because after listening to The Discovery and TWDA, I thought the band had a niche of sweeping over polyrhythmic chugs, so this was a interesting change. I always liked the sweeping, so i could have used more of it though. Simarilly to TWDA, not many of the tracks really stood out to me. I remember enjoying Tidebinder and Resilience (awesome sweeps in the beginning). Throw Me In the Jungle is a joke. Don't know what they were thinking with that one. The Louder the Sound, the More We All Believe was a pretty different sounding song, and I enjoyed it.

Basically this album seemed to turn out the same way TWDA did for me, where it isn't bad, but nothing stands out. Unlike that album however, this one moved farther away from their deathcore sound, and did stuff a little bit differently. I think this album will grow on me the more I listen to it. And I love this album's cover art (and all the other ones too).

I rate this album a 6.5/10 and my favorite track is Resilience

Didn't see VOAT had a Djent subverse, I also didn't know BoO realeased a new album, it's good day today!

Pardon any typo's and crap spelling!

I definitely miss the constant sweeping and tapping throught the entire album, it almost feels like a new band. In general I don't think this album hit as hard as their others. It's still heavy, but the blast strumming kinda falls behind and mixes in with the vocals for a lot of the tracks. Another thing that bugged me was that all the songs chug allong at roughly the same tone, maybe float around that lower string while blast strumming to mix it up a bit. It kinda made the album sound like one long song with occasional riff breaks.

Free Fall was a very nice song, it mixed different guitar styles together rather than just keeping constant chugging, sick bells too! This is one of my favorites from the album, if this was a single release I'd throw some money down on it. Illuminate was quite nice but I'm really not a fan of mixing clean-ish happy bits in a growly harsh song, but some people do so it was nice they included it.

The Sleeping and the Dead has such a beatiful bouncy guitar backing, it stood out for me, there was also some level 99 wizadry strumming patterns going on. It then fell over into Tidebinder which was a really stunning track for the most part, there was some arsey soft bit which I didnt like. Personal opinions and whatnot! The guitar strumming in Tidebinder was A++ though, it stood out unlike in the other songs.

Resilience has some lovely flicky sweepy guitar bits, but there was something about it that just didnt roll right. It reminded me of Chelsea Grin's new stuff, I do like both bands but it just put me off this song. Goddess of the Dawn was allright, nothing special, it sounded like the rest of the album. The Louder the Sound, the More We All Believe was the same; it had nice bits but again nothing special imo.

Warlords had a stunning Vildhjarta-esque intro and slid into something lovely. I really enjoyed this song, the mastering was proper nice here and that use of killswitch (or whatever they used) was a lovely change. It started to sound like Killswitch engage in the middle, kinda weird but nice. The solo was fucking beautiful.

The last two songs didn't really do anything for me, that dance outro was cool and reminded me of The Browning's old stuff

Overall it was a nice album, I'd listen to it again easy. I wouldn't buy the album but I'd single out Warlords, Free Fall and Tidebinder as the nicest. I'll probably pick them up as singles.

A good 7/10, I still miss Jason Richardson, they've done very well without him though.
